column1: unit-oracle|What makes a unit test's oracle independent of the implementation?|The oracle encodes an externally justified expected behavior, invariant, or known result rather than copying the same algorithm. Isolate the smallest useful behavior and test observable outputs and failures. A test that merely mirrors implementation steps can reproduce the same bug.|oracle;independent~invariant;observable;bug|Copying production code into a test guarantees an independent oracle.|A sorting test uses the production sorter again to compute its expected result. Improve the oracle.|Check monotonic order and preservation of the input multiset, plus small known examples. This tests properties without duplicating the same sorting routine.|hypothesis,sre-testing|test

integration|What should an integration test verify that mocks alone cannot?|Verify real component contracts at a boundary, such as database transaction behavior, serialization, authentication configuration, or a broker/client interaction. Control fixtures and cleanup, and inject failures. Mock tests are useful but do not prove the real protocol or schema is compatible.|boundary~contract;real;fixture~cleanup;failure|A mocked database test proves the actual database isolation behavior.|An ORM unit test passes but a migration breaks production queries. Design an integration test.|Start the supported database version with the actual migration, seed boundary data, run real queries and transactions, and assert schema/constraint behavior and cleanup.|sre-testing,postgres|integration

end-to-end|What should an end-to-end test assert in an AI screen-to-answer application?|Exercise capture, extraction, prompt assembly, model transport, and rendering through real interfaces, using controlled screen and model fixtures where needed. Assert that the lower code reaches the answer request and that stale results cannot replace a newer task; record failures at each boundary.|capture;extract~prompt;render;stale~newer|A screenshot of an answer card proves the original code reached the model.|How would you detect a regression where only a top question is read while lower code is dropped?|Render a known split-layout fixture, exercise the actual read path, inspect the downstream request for the code/operators, and compare the visible answer against a trusted oracle. Distinguish extraction success from answer correctness.|sre-testing,node-test|end-to-end

properties|How do property-based tests go beyond a large set of hand-picked examples?|Generate inputs from a controlled domain, assert invariants or metamorphic relations, and shrink failures to smaller counterexamples. Persist failing examples or seeds for replay. Properties must be justified; random input alone is not an oracle.|generat;invariant~property;shrink;seed~replay|Random inputs alone establish that an algorithm is correct.|Design a property-based test for a serializer/deserializer pair and identify a weak property.|Round-trip supported values and compare against documented normalization, but also test an independent schema or decoder because paired matching bugs can pass a round-trip. Include invalid and boundary inputs.|hypothesis|stateful

fake-clocks|How should fake clocks be used to test retries without sleeping in real time?|Inject the clock and scheduler, advance simulated time explicitly, and assert attempt counts, deadlines, and backoff boundaries. Control randomness or inject jitter samples. Distinguish wall-clock time from monotonic elapsed time and ensure pending promises are flushed as required.|inject~fake;advance;deadline;jitter~random|Sleeping for a long time is the only way to verify retry deadlines.|A test advances Date.now but retry timers do not fire. What abstraction is missing?|The scheduling mechanism was not controlled alongside the time source. Inject or mock timers as well as the clock and flush the appropriate asynchronous work deterministically.|node-test|timers

scheduler|What does a deterministic scheduler contribute to concurrency testing?|It controls when operations yield or resume so a known interleaving can be reproduced and competing schedules explored. Assert state invariants and progress properties, record schedule decisions, and distinguish deterministic simulation from proof over all possible schedules.|interleav~schedule;reproduc;invariant;all~coverage|Testing one deterministic schedule proves every concurrent execution safe.|How can a test reproduce a stale asynchronous response overwriting newer state?|Delay the first operation, complete a newer one, then release the old response. Assert a generation/version check rejects the stale result and record that schedule as a regression.|sre-testing,hypothesis|deterministic

record-replay|What must a useful record/replay harness capture, and what are its limits?|Capture relevant external inputs, ordering, time/randomness, environment versions, and protocol data with secrets redacted. Replay against a defined oracle. A recording preserves observed behavior but is not evidence that the observed output was correct or that unseen schedules are safe.|input;order~time;redact~secret;oracle|Recorded production output is automatically a correct reference answer.|A replay passes after an API contract changed because the old recording contains the old bug. How should the harness improve?|Version recordings, verify the oracle against the contract, add semantic assertions, and refresh fixtures deliberately rather than accepting replay equality as correctness.|sre-testing,hypothesis|test

fault-injection|How should a fault-injection test specify its scope and oracle?|Name the injected fault, its location and timing, expected recovery/degradation, and bounded progress deadline. Inject timeouts, dropped connections, duplicate events, or partial failures in a controlled environment. Verify invariants and observability, not merely that an exception occurred.|fault;timing~location;invariant;deadline~bounded|A test that throws any exception proves recovery works.|Design a test for a crash between a side-effect commit and message acknowledgment.|Commit the state, interrupt before acknowledgment, redeliver, and assert that deduplication prevents a second mutation. Verify retry/recovery metrics and eventual acknowledgment.|sre-testing,aws-idempotency|failure

state-machine|How does state-machine testing help test a circuit breaker or interview session?|Define states, allowed transitions, inputs, and invariants; generate sequences and compare observed transitions with the model. Check invalid transitions and recovery paths. Model state is an independent specification, not a copy of hidden implementation flags.|state;transition;sequence;invariant|Testing each public method once covers every state-machine behavior.|Design a breaker test covering open, half-open, recovery, and a failed probe.|Use a fake clock and controlled failures, assert thresholds open the breaker, only bounded probes are admitted, success closes it, and a failed probe reopens it.|hypothesis|state machine

deadlock-livelock|How do deadlock and livelock differ, and how can tests detect them?|Deadlock prevents progress because participants wait on one another; livelock involves ongoing activity without useful progress. Use explicit progress counters, bounded deadlines, state/lock traces, and controlled schedules. A timeout indicates missing progress but does not alone identify the cause.|wait~deadlock;activity~livelock;progress;trace~schedule|High CPU use proves a process cannot be stuck.|Two workers repeatedly release and retry conflicting reservations without completing. What should the test detect?|Observe active transitions but no completed operation within a bounded schedule/time budget. Capture the repeated states and test a coordination or randomized-backoff policy for progress.|sre-testing,hypothesis|failure

race|How can a regression test demonstrate a race instead of relying on lucky timing?|Insert explicit barriers or controllable promises at the shared-state boundary, run the conflicting operations in a chosen order, and assert the violated invariant or lost update. Repeat alternative schedules and record the one that failed; avoid arbitrary sleeps as the primary synchronization.|barrier~promise;order~interleav;invariant;arbitrary~sleep|Running a concurrency test once without failure proves absence of races.|Two requests both read cache version 1 before either writes version 2. How can you force and test stale publication?|Pause both after read, complete the newer mutation, then release the stale writer. Assert compare-and-set/version logic rejects it and that the final state is the newer value.|hypothesis,sre-testing|state

model-based|What is the difference between a model-based oracle and implementation duplication?|A model encodes a simpler specification of allowed state and behavior, often with different data structures. Generate actions, execute both systems, and compare externally meaningful results and invariants. Validate the model itself with known cases and review assumptions.|specification;action~operation;invariant;independent~simpler|A model that copies production internals is automatically an independent oracle.|How would you model-test an LRU cache without copying its linked-list implementation?|Use a simple ordered list or map as a specification, generate get/put/evict sequences, and compare returned values, capacity, and recency behavior after each action.|hypothesis|model

regression|What should a regression test preserve after fixing a bug?|Preserve the minimal triggering input or schedule and the intended externally observable behavior. Add a boundary or contrasting nonfailure case so the fix is not just a special case. A regression test should fail on the old implementation for the targeted reason.|trigger~reproduc;old;observable;boundary|A test added after a fix is useful even if it never fails on the old code.|A copied-question guard rejects hello as a valid greeting reply. What regression cases are needed?|Check greeting-to-greeting succeeds, an actual copied technical question fails, a substantive answer succeeds, and retry/cancellation behavior remains bounded. This isolates the false-positive boundary.|node-test,sre-testing|test

boundaries|How should boundary conditions be derived systematically?|Start from the domain and invariants, then test empty, singleton, minimum/maximum, invalid, and transition-adjacent values. Include overflow, Unicode, time boundaries, and resource limits when relevant. Expected behavior must be specified rather than inferred from the current output.|empty;maximum~minimum;invalid;invariant|Typical happy-path examples cover every important boundary.|Design boundary tests for a paginated API with an optional cursor and a page limit.|Test absent/invalid/expired cursor, zero/negative/excessive limits, empty and exact-boundary datasets, stable tie ordering, tenant binding, and concurrent inserts under the declared consistency policy.|sre-testing,hypothesis|test

flaky-oracles|How can false-positive evaluation oracles damage an AI application's quality claims?|Keyword overlap can reward a fluent wrong answer or reject a valid paraphrase. Separate deterministic evidence checks from semantic review, test negations and contradictions, use trusted references, and report uncertainty. An aggregate score must not override a serious factual error.|keyword~paraphrase;contradict~negation;reference;serious~factual|A keyword score of 95 percent proves semantic correctness.|An answer says Arc makes every inner type thread-safe yet contains all required keywords. How should an evaluator handle it?|Flag the false claim as a critical factual failure regardless of weighted coverage, cite the Send/Sync restriction, and request independent review or a corrected reference-grounded explanation.|rust-send,hypothesis|Sync
